questions.question: Examine the interrelationship between migration and urban social disorganisation.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine the interrelationship between migration and urban social disorganisation.
  • Migration as a Cause of Urban Social Disorganisation (6 mark)
  • a) Rapid population growth- Influx of migrants leads to overcrowding in cities.
  • b) Housing shortages and slums- Migrants often settle in informal settlements with poor conditions.
  • c) Pressure on urban infrastructure- Overburdened water supply, sanitation, transport, and
  • healthcare systems.
  • d) Unemployment and informal sector growth- Limited job opportunities push migrants into
  • insecure work.
  • e) Cultural heterogeneity- Diverse backgrounds may lead to cultural clashes and weak social
  • cohesion.
  • f) Weak social control- Absence of strong community bonds increases deviant behaviour.
  • Urban Social Disorganisation Affecting Migrants (5 mark)
  • a) Social exclusion and marginalization- Migrants face discrimination and lack of integration.
  • b) Poor living conditions- Slums lack basic amenities, affecting health and dignity.
  • c) Crime and insecurity- Disorganised environments often see higher crime rates.
  • d) Family disintegration- Migration may separate families or create stress within them.
  • e) Limited access to services- Education, healthcare, and welfare services are often inaccessible.
  • Interrelationship (Two-way Process)
  • a) Cycle of poverty- Migration leads to urban poverty, which reinforces disorganisation. (4 mark)
  • b) Mutual reinforcement- Disorganisation attracts vulnerable migrants and worsens conditions.
  • c) Strain on governance- Urban institutions struggle to manage growing populations.
  • d) Impact on sustainable development- Unplanned growth undermines long-term urban stability. .
questions.final_answer: Option Rapid population growth- Influx of migrants leads to overcrowding in cities.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Estimate the effectiveness of livelihood promotion strategies in enhancing rural income.
questions.solution_html:

  • Effectiveness of Livelihood Promotion Strategies (10 marks)
  • a) Income generation opportunities- Provide sustainable sources of income through self
  • employment and wage employment.
  • b) Diversification of livelihoods- Reduce dependence on agriculture by promoting non-farm
  • activities like small enterprises and services.
  • c) Skill development and capacity building- Training programmes enhance employability and
  • productivity.
  • d) Promotion of micro-enterprises- Encourages rural entrepreneurship and local economic growth.
  • e) Access to credit and financial inclusion- Microfinance and banking services help the poor invest
  • in income-generating activities.
  • f) Strengthening Self-Help Groups (SHGs)- SHGs promote savings, credit access, and collective
  • economic activities.
  • g) Women empowerment- Increases women’s participation in economic activities and decision
  • making.
  • h) Improved market linkages- Better access to markets helps in getting fair prices for products.
  • i) Reduction in poverty levels- Increased income contributes to better living standards.
  • j) Employment generation- Reduces unemployment and underemployment in rural areas.
questions.final_answer: Option Income generation opportunities- Provide sustainable sources of income through self

• Examine the causes and consequences of agrarian distress. - / -(5 marks)
  • Causes
  •  Dependence on monsoon and climate uncertainties.
  •  Rising cost of inputs (seeds, fertilizers, irrigation).
  •  Indebtedness due to lack of institutional credit.
  • Consequences
  •  Increase in farmer poverty and migration.
  •  Extreme cases leading to farmer suicides and social instability.
questions.final_answer:  Extreme cases leading to farmer suicides and social instability
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Illustrate the Nagarapalika Act provisions to urban local administration.
questions.solution_html:
• (74th Constitutional Amendment Act)
  •  Establishes Urban Local Bodies (Municipalities) for governance.

  •  Ensures devolution of powers and responsibilities.
  •  Includes reservation for women and weaker sections.
  •  Assigns functions like urban planning, sanitation, water supply.
questions.final_answer:  Assigns functions like urban planning, sanitation, water supply

questions.question: Examine the interrelationship between migration and urban social disorganisation.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine the interrelationship between migration and urban social disorganisation.
  • Migration as a Cause of Urban Social Disorganisation (6 mark)
  • a) Rapid population growth- Influx of migrants leads to overcrowding in cities.
  • b) Housing shortages and slums- Migrants often settle in informal settlements with poor conditions.
  • c) Pressure on urban infrastructure- Overburdened water supply, sanitation, transport, and
  • healthcare systems.
  • d) Unemployment and informal sector growth- Limited job opportunities push migrants into
  • insecure work.
  • e) Cultural heterogeneity- Diverse backgrounds may lead to cultural clashes and weak social
  • cohesion.
  • f) Weak social control- Absence of strong community bonds increases deviant behaviour.
  • Urban Social Disorganisation Affecting Migrants (5 mark)
  • a) Social exclusion and marginalization- Migrants face discrimination and lack of integration.
  • b) Poor living conditions- Slums lack basic amenities, affecting health and dignity.
  • c) Crime and insecurity- Disorganised environments often see higher crime rates.
  • d) Family disintegration- Migration may separate families or create stress within them.
  • e) Limited access to services- Education, healthcare, and welfare services are often inaccessible.
  • Interrelationship (Two-way Process)
  • a) Cycle of poverty- Migration leads to urban poverty, which reinforces disorganisation. (4 mark)
  • b) Mutual reinforcement- Disorganisation attracts vulnerable migrants and worsens conditions.
  • c) Strain on governance- Urban institutions struggle to manage growing populations.
  • d) Impact on sustainable development- Unplanned growth undermines long-term urban stability. .
questions.final_answer: Option Rapid population growth- Influx of migrants leads to overcrowding in cities.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Estimate the effectiveness of livelihood promotion strategies in enhancing rural income.
questions.solution_html:
• Estimate the effectiveness of livelihood promotion strategies in enhancing rural income
  • Effectiveness of Livelihood Promotion Strategies (10 marks)
  • a) Income generation opportunities- Provide sustainable sources of income through self
  • employment and wage employment.
  • b) Diversification of livelihoods- Reduce dependence on agriculture by promoting non-farm
  • activities like small enterprises and services.
  • c) Skill development and capacity building- Training programmes enhance employability and
  • productivity.
  • d) Promotion of micro-enterprises- Encourages rural entrepreneurship and local economic growth.
  • e) Access to credit and financial inclusion- Microfinance and banking services help the poor invest
  • in income-generating activities.
  • f) Strengthening Self-Help Groups (SHGs)- SHGs promote savings, credit access, and collective
  • economic activities.
  • g) Women empowerment- Increases women’s participation in economic activities and decision
  • making.
  • h) Improved market linkages- Better access to markets helps in getting fair prices for products.
  • i) Reduction in poverty levels- Increased income contributes to better living standards.
  • j) Employment generation- Reduces unemployment and underemployment in rural areas.
questions.final_answer: Option Income generation opportunities- Provide sustainable sources of income through self
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
